skeleton.finalText:
I wrote the contract in `src/index.ts`, and `npm run build` finishes with no errors. The build also produced `src/index.js`, which I deleted so `src/index.ts` is the only file I added.

Where the spec left things open, I made these choices:

- **Two functions.** `isDigestDue(timeZone, now)` answers whether it is Monday in the organization's time zone. `buildDigest({ timeZone, tasks, now })` builds the list of open tasks. `buildDigest` doesn't check the day itself; the caller decides that with `isDigestDue`.
- **Unknown time zone.** The spec doesn't say which call refuses "Mars/Olympus", so the doc comments say both functions throw an error naming the time zone. Both test writers will see the same rule.
- **No open tasks.** `buildDigest` returns `null` rather than an empty digest.
- **Times are `Date` objects**, and "now" is always passed in by the caller.
- **Gates.** A submission's gate is `1 | 2 | 3`. A task's furthest gate is `0 | 1 | 2 | 3`, with 0 meaning no submissions.
- **Fields in each listed task.** Each entry carries `id`, `title`, `ageDays`, `submissions` (a count), `furthestGate` and `stalled`. The field names are my choice; the spec only describes what they hold.

Exports: `TaskStatus`, `Gate`, `FurthestGate`, `Submission`, `Task`, `DigestInput`, `DigestEntry`, `Digest`, `isDigestDue`, `buildDigest`

public.finalText:
I've written the public test suite in four files under `tests/public/`. `npm run build` reports no errors. All 28 tests fail when run, as expected, because the function bodies still throw `not implemented`.

Each scenario has a happy-path test and at least one boundary test:

- **`due.test.ts`**:
  - `[happy-1]` Singapore: due at Monday 00:30 and at exactly Monday 00:00:00; not due at Sunday 23:59:59.
  - `[boundary-1]` New York after the clocks went forward: due at Monday 00:30 and at Monday 00:00:00; not due at Sunday 23:59:59.
  - `[unhappy-2]` `isDigestDue` with `"Mars/Olympus"` throws an error that names the zone.
- **`listing.test.ts`**:
  - `[happy-2]` A task is listed with age, submission count and furthest gate. Also checked: furthest gate is 0 with no submissions, it's the highest gate reached rather than the latest one, and merged tasks are left out.
  - `[boundary-2]` Exactly 10 days gives age 10. Both 9 days 23 hours and one millisecond short of 10 days give age 9.
- **`stalled.test.ts`**:
  - `[boundary-3]` Stalled at exactly 14 days, whether counted from the latest submission or from posting. Not stalled at 13 days 23 hours. Not stalled when posted 30 days ago with a submission 2 days ago.
  - `[happy-3]` Stalled tasks come first, older first within each group. A newer stalled task still comes before an older one that isn't stalled. Tasks of the same age are ordered by id.
- **`subject.test.ts`**:
  - `[happy-4]` Subject reads "5 open tasks, 2 stalled", and "1 open task, 0 stalled" for a single task. Merged tasks aren't counted.
  - `[unhappy-1]` Returns `null` when every task is merged, and when there are no tasks at all.
  - `[unhappy-2]` `buildDigest` with an unknown zone throws an error that names it.

All tests use a fixed `now` of `2026-03-11T12:00:00Z`. I didn't test two things the spec leaves open:
- **Order within one age:** for tasks with the same age in days but different posting times, "older" could mean either value, so tasks that tie on age in my tests share the exact same posting time.
- **Unknown zone, nothing open:** the spec doesn't say whether that case throws or returns `null`.

Building writes compiled `.js` files next to the sources, including `src/index.js`. I deleted them afterwards so nothing is left outside `tests/public/`.

28 tests, in 4 files.

private.finalText:
I wrote 83 tests in 7 files under `tests/private/`. `npm run build` reports no errors. All 83 fail against the current stubs, and each unknown-time-zone test checks that the error message contains the zone's name.

To check the tests themselves, I ran them in a scratch copy of the project against a correct reference implementation of my own. All 83 passed there, along with the 28 public tests. I then deleted the `.js` files the build had created in `src/`, `tests/public/` and `tests/private/`, so nothing changed outside `tests/private/`.

The cases a shortcut built to pass the public suite would get wrong:

- **Due on Monday:** checking the day in UTC or the machine's clock, or assuming one fixed New York offset all year. The tests cover winter, the November clock change, London, Sydney, offsets of half and quarter hours, ±14/−11 hours, the end of Monday and every other weekday.
- **Age and stalled:** counting local calendar days instead of 24-hour periods. Across New York's clock change, ten calendar days is only 9 days 23 hours, so the age is 9. Rounding instead of rounding down, and the millisecond either side of 14 days, are also covered.
- **Latest submission and furthest gate:** taking the first or last submission in the list instead of the latest or highest.
- **Order:** sorting by latest submission instead of posting time, or relying on input order when two tasks tie and should be ordered by id.
- **Subject:** hardcoded strings, "1 stalled", and merged tasks that look stalled.
- **Unknown time zone:** names other than `Mars/Olympus`.

The public `buildDigest` tests use a Wednesday as `now`. I didn't count that as open, because the interface gives "no task is open" as its only reason to return null, but my tests use a Monday so they hold either way.

83 tests, in 7 files.

Open in the spec: none

notes.finalText:
I've written `notes.md`, grouped into six areas: when the digest is due, which tasks are listed, the entry fields, the stalled rule, the order of the list, and the subject.

Some details are easy to miss:
- **Order:** within each group, the order follows how long ago the task was posted, not its latest activity.
- **Subject:** "task" becomes singular when only one task is open, but "stalled" never changes.
- **Time zones:** the New York cases use a Monday right after the clocks went forward.
- **Ties:** tasks posted at the same moment are ordered by id. The ticket's interface says tasks of the same age, but every example of a tie has identical posting times, so the note only claims the identical-time case.

18 bullets.
